- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the forecast slightly to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward bias — allow for slight mean reversion.  
- If forecast overshoots a recent peak (e.g., >10% above prior 7-day high), apply a 5–10% downward correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show strong downward momentum, model should not overcorrect upward — expect mean reversion within 10–15 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.25) and forecast is erratic, smooth the curve — avoid sharp swings in 3–5 day windows.  
- When sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.5–0.7) and price is near a 30-day low, model should not underestimate recovery — expect a modest upward bias.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3 consecutive days, check for lag — adjust for 1–2 day delay in price reaction.  
- For sentiment >0.7, avoid forecasting below 5% below recent 14-day average — model should be conservative but not pessimistic.
